title: Reading Drill — Keeping track of school costumes — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Keeping track of school costumes — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Millcross, work on costumes being loaned out while repairs are pending had already produced a small collection of wardrobe logs. The school wardrobe organiser used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the number of unusable returns.

**B** The group kept repair tags visible from the shelf for the new trial, which was planned to run for three weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that unrecorded exchanges should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
